svg.title: Four cost levers, in the order to try them — and how to pick by bottleneck
svg.desc: Four numbered cards in the order to reach for them. One, trim the retrieved context: cut top k and chunk size, the highest impact and lowest effort, with the risk that if the relevant chunk sat at rank four you just lost it, so check MRR after every cut. Two, caching: provider-side prompt caching bills a repeated static prefix at a fraction of the input price, while semantic caching in your own vector store eliminates the call entirely on a hit — completely different mechanisms, not two names for one thing. Three, the Batch API: about fifty percent off for anything not real-time and tolerant of up to twenty-four hours, which is exactly what an offline evaluation run is. Four, model routing, deliberately last, because the complexity classifier itself costs tokens and latency and is a new component that can fail or misroute. Below the cards, a strip on picking by bottleneck: input-bound workloads want trimming and caching, easy-query-heavy traffic wants routing, and latency-tolerant bulk work wants the Batch API.
svg.text: Four levers, in the order to try them
cut top_k and chunk_size — highest impact, lowest effort, and it attacks the pile that dominates the bill
risk: if the answer chunk sat at rank 4, you just deleted it — check MRR after every cut
Caching — two different mechanisms, not two names for one
prompt caching: provider-side, automatic, bills the repeated static prefix at a fraction — reduces input cost
semantic caching: your vector store, embed-and-lookup — eliminates the call entirely on a hit
~50% off for anything not real-time, up to 24h — right for eval runs and backfills, wrong for live support
a cheap model for the easy paths sounds like the obvious first move…
…but the complexity classifier costs tokens and latency, and it's a new component that can fail or misroute
